facts.statement: Ferrodraco had an estimated wingspan of about 4 meters.
facts.quote: Its wingspan was estimated to be about 4 m.

facts.statement: The holotype of Ferrodraco was discovered in April 2017 by cattle farmer Robert A. Elliott while spraying herbicide.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen was initially discovered in April 2017 when cattle farmer Robert A. Elliott was spraying herbicide near Belmont Station.

facts.statement: Ferrodraco lentoni was named and described in 2019 by a team led by Adele H. Pentland.
facts.quote: In 2019, the type species Ferrodraco lentoni was named and described by Adele H. Pentland, Stephen Francis Poropat, Travis R. Tischler, Trish Sloan, Robert A. Elliott, Harry A. Elliott, Judy A. Elliott and David A. Elliott.

facts.statement: Ferrodraco weighed approximately 10 kilograms.
facts.quote: Ferrodraco had a wingspan of 4 m and weighed 10 kg.

facts.statement: Ferrodraco had a premaxillary crest that rose at a 60-degree angle to a rounded top.
facts.quote: The snout bears a premaxillary crest, the front edge of which continues the line of the snout tip, steeply rising under an angle of 60 degrees, and ending in a rounded crest top.

facts.statement: The skull of Ferrodraco was estimated to be about 60 centimeters long.
facts.quote: The length of the skull has been estimated to be about 60 cm.

facts.statement: The crest on Ferrodraco's snout was very thin, measuring only 4 millimeters in thickness.
facts.quote: The crest is very thin transversely however, only up to 4 mm thick.

facts.statement: Ferrodraco had a total of fifty teeth in its head, with twelve in the upper jaw and thirteen in the lower jaw.
facts.quote: There is an estimated total of twelve teeth in the upper jaw and thirteen teeth in the lower jaw for a total of fifty in the head as a whole.

facts.statement: A 2022 study confirmed that Ferrodraco belongs to the family Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: In 2022, Pentland et al. published a detailed description of Ferrodraco (particularly the post-cranial skeleton) and a renewed phylogenetic appraisal that unequivocally demonstrated that it belongs in the family Anhangueridae as proposed by Holgado and Pêgas.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest that the exact position of Ferrodraco within Anhangueridae remains uncertain.
facts.quote: This study suggested that the precise position of Ferrodraco and Mythunga within Anhangueridae still remains uncertain, and that the diversity of Australian pterosaur fauna has been greatly underestimated.

facts.statement: Ferrodraco had a unique trait where the first tooth pair in the snout and lower jaws was smaller than the other front teeth.
facts.quote: The first tooth pair in both the premaxillae of the snout and in the front lower jaws is smaller than the other front teeth.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen was discovered in April 2017 by farmer Robert A. Elliott while spraying herbicide near the Belmont station.
facts.quote: El espécimen holotipo se descubrió inicialmente en abril de 2017 cuando el ganadero Robert A. Elliott estaba rociando herbicida cerca de la estación de Belmont.

facts.statement: The species Ferrodraco lentoni was named and described in 2019 by a team led by Adele H. Pentland and including Stephen Francis Poropat, Travis R. Tischler, Trish Sloan, and the Elliott family.
facts.quote: En 2019, la especie tipo Ferrodraco lentoni fue nombrada y descrita por Adele H. Pentland, Stephen Francis Poropat, Travis R. Tischler, Trish Sloan, Robert A. Elliott, Harry A. Elliott, Judy A. Elliott y David A. Elliott.

facts.statement: The generic name derives from the Latin words for 'iron' and 'dragon', referring to the fact that the skeleton was found in ironstone.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del latín ferrum, "hierro", y draco, "dragón", en referencia al hecho de que el esqueleto se encontró en piedra de hierro.

facts.statement: The specific name honors the late mayor of Winton Shire, Graham Thomas 'Butch' Lenton, for his community work and support of the Australian Age of Dinosaurs, who died in 2017.
facts.quote: El nombre específico honra al difunto alcalde de Winton Shire, Graham Thomas 'Butch' Lenton, por su trabajo para la comunidad local y su apoyo a la Era Australiana de los Dinosaurios, quien murió en 2017.

facts.statement: The holotype was found in the Winton Formation dating to the lower Cenomanian-Turonian, approximately 96 million years ago.
facts.quote: El holotipo, AODF 876, se encontró en una capa de la Formación Winton que data del Cenomaniense - Turoniense inferior, de unos 96 millones de años.

facts.statement: The fossil consists of a partial skeleton including the skull and lower jaws.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto parcial con cráneo y mandíbulas inferiores.

facts.statement: The specimen represents a fully developed but immature animal.
facts.quote: Representa un animal completamente desarrollado pero aún no maduro.

facts.statement: The skeleton is largely preserved in three dimensions due to the ironstone, though some bones have been crushed.
facts.quote: El esqueleto se ha conservado en gran parte tridimensionalmente debido a la piedra de hierro, pero algunos huesos, sin embargo, se han aplastado.

facts.statement: The wingspan of Ferrodraco is estimated to be 4 meters.
facts.quote: La envergadura de Ferrodraco se estimó en 4 metros.

facts.statement: The first pair of teeth in the premaxillae points vertically and is slightly offset upward from the jawline.
facts.quote: El primer par de dientes en los premaxilares se dirige verticalmente y está ligeramente desplazado hacia arriba desde la línea de la mandíbula.

facts.statement: The snout features a premaxillary crest where the front edge continues the snout tip line, rising abruptly at a 60-degree angle to end in a rounded crest.
facts.quote: El hocico tiene una cresta premaxilar, cuyo borde frontal continúa la línea de la punta del hocico, elevándose abruptamente en un ángulo de 60 grados y terminando en una cresta redondeada.

facts.statement: The skull length is estimated to be about 60 centimeters.
facts.quote: Se ha estimado que la longitud del cráneo es de unos 60 centímetros.

facts.statement: The crest is very thin transversely, measuring only up to 4 millimeters in thickness.
facts.quote: La cresta es muy delgada transversalmente, solo mide hasta 4 milímetros de espesor.

facts.statement: The crest has a base length of 131 millimeters and a height of 128 millimeters.
facts.quote: La cresta tiene una longitud de base de 131 milímetros y una altura de 128 milímetros.

facts.statement: There are an estimated twelve teeth in the upper jaw and thirteen in the lower jaw, totaling fifty teeth in the head.
facts.quote: Hay un total estimado de doce dientes en la mandíbula superior y trece dientes en la mandíbula inferior para un total de cincuenta en la cabeza como un todo.

facts.statement: Ferrodraco was the youngest known member of the clade Anhangueria, proving that the clade did not go extinct during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Ferrodraco fue el miembro más joven conocido del clado Anhangueria, y prueba que el clado no se extinguió durante el Cretácico superior.

facts.statement: One phylogenetic analysis placed Ferrodraco within the clade Ornithocheirae, specifically in the subfamily Ornithocheirinae as the sister species to Mythunga, another Australian pterosaur from older layers.
facts.quote: El primer análisis ubicó a Ferrodraco dentro del clado Ornithocheirae, más precisamente dentro de la subfamilia Ornithocheirinae como la especie hermana de Mythunga, otro pterosaurio australiano de capas algo más antiguas.

facts.statement: A more recent 2020 study by Borja Holgado and Rodrigo Pêgas placed Ferrodraco within the family Anhangueridae, specifically in the subfamily Tropeognathinae, though it remains the sister taxon to Mythunga.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un estudio más reciente realizado en 2020 por Borja Holgado y Rodrigo Pêgas colocó a Ferrodraco dentro de la familia Anhangueridae, más específicamente dentro de la subfamilia Tropeognathinae, aunque sigue siendo el taxón hermano de Mythunga.

facts.statement: Ferrodraco belongs to the parent group Tropeognathinae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Tropeognathinae

facts.statement: Ferrodraco is classified in the family Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: Family: Anhangueridae

facts.statement: Ferrodraco is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: Ferrodraco lived from the Cenomanian to the Turonian, between 100.5 and 89.8 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Turonian (100.5 to 89.8 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether a 2010 report of an ornithocheirid jaw fragment from Australia represents a younger species, as the Molecap Greensand layers where it was found may date to a time younger than Ferrodraco.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, en 2010, un fragmento de mandíbula de ornitoqueírido que incluye dos dientes (espécimen WAM 68.5.11) había sido reportado en Australia, el mismo lugar donde se encontró Ferrodraco, y este espécimen fue desenterrado en Molecap Greensand, capas que posiblemente tienen una edad aún más joven que Ferrodraco.
